usage.goal: Recognize and use common fruits vocabulary in practical everyday situations.
usage.canDoStatement: I can understand and use common fruits words in a simple situation

scenes.scenario: At the market, Jo chooses an apple for lunch, a banana for breakfast, and an orange for juice.
scenes.imageBrief: An adult shopper placing an apple with lunch items, a banana with breakfast items, and oranges beside a juicer.

scenes.scenario: The fruit salad has grapes and strawberries, and a large watermelon is ready to slice.

check.question: Which fruit is ready to slice?

scenes.imageBrief: A fruit-salad bowl with grapes and strawberries beside a whole watermelon and a safe cutting area.

scenes.scenario: Mina buys a pineapple and a mango, then chooses a soft peach to eat today.

check.question: Which fruit will Mina eat today?

scenes.imageBrief: An adult shopper holding a ripe peach, with a pineapple and mango already in the shopping basket.

scenes.scenario: A pear is in the lunch box, while blueberries and raspberries top the yogurt.

check.question: What is in the lunch box?

scenes.imageBrief: A pear inside an open lunch box, with separate blueberries and raspberries on a bowl of yogurt.

scenes.scenario: The baker decorates one tart with blackberries, one with cranberries, and one with gooseberries.

check.question: Which berries are on the first tart?

scenes.imageBrief: Three separate fruit tarts: the first with blackberries, the second with cranberries, and the third with gooseberries, without labels.

reading.title: Fruit for the Week
reading.text: Jo shops for fruit on Sunday. He buys bananas for breakfast and apples for lunch. He chooses oranges for juice and a grape and strawberry for a fruit salad. At home, he slices a watermelon, packs a pear, and adds a blueberry and raspberry to yogurt. A baker uses a blackberry, cranberry, and gooseberry in three tarts.
reading.imageBrief: Show the main adult everyday situation from “Fruit for the Week” with the key objects clearly visible, naturally arranged, and free of written labels.

exercises.prompt: Which fruit is for breakfast?
Which fruit is ready to slice?
Which fruit will Mina eat today?
What is in the lunch box?
Which berries are on the first tart?
Use “Apple” in one short sentence about an everyday situation.
exercises.answer: At the market, Jo chooses an apple for lunch, a banana for breakfast, and an orange for juice.

exercises.prompt: Name another lesson word that can be used with “Blackberry” in the same situation.

video.title: Fruits 1: Words in Action
video.idea: A 30–50 second adult everyday scene based on the curated lesson situations. Show each target naturally, pause for one context question, then model the answer in a complete sentence.
video.scriptStarter: At the market, Jo chooses an apple for lunch, a banana for breakfast, and an orange for juice.

reading.title: A Fruit-Tasting Market
reading.text: Nina visits a market with fruit from many regions. She tries mulberry, boysenberry, and acai berry in a smoothie. A seller displays lingonberry and elderberry beside papaya. reading.title: Choosing Citrus and Stone Fruit
reading.text: Salma buys lemon and lime for cooking, plus grapefruit for breakfast. She compares a small kumquat with a large pomelo. At another stall, she chooses cherries, plums, apricots, and nectarines. Before leaving, she adds a box of dates for quick snacks.
reading.imageBrief: Show the main adult everyday situation from “Choosing Citrus and Stone Fruit” with the key objects clearly visible, naturally arranged, and free of written labels.

usage.goal: Recognize common fruits and use them in simple food and shopping contexts.

scenes.scenario: At the market, I can choose a fig, an olive, an avocado.

check.question: Which word is shown in the picture?

scenes.imageBrief: Create one clear Pre-A1 visual for fruits that represents: At the market, I can choose a fig, an olive, an avocado. Emphasize fig, olive, and avocado and avoid clutter.

scenes.scenario: At the market, I can choose a persimmon, a pomegranate.

check.question: Which word is shown in the picture?

scenes.imageBrief: Create one clear Pre-A1 visual for fruits that represents: At the market, I can choose a persimmon, a pomegranate. Emphasize persimmon and pomegranate and avoid clutter.

reading.title: Fruits Mini Story
reading.text: Today I am at the market. I see fig, olive, and avocado. I also find persimmon and pomegranate. I choose a few things and put them in my bag. Then I practice the new English words while I shop. We also remember earlier words such as lemon and lime.
reading.imageBrief: One uncluttered fruits scene supporting the reading and showing the first six target words.

exercises.prompt: Image Recognition: Which word best matches the picture?
Image Recognition: Which word best matches the picture?
Reading Comprehension: Which word comes first in this lesson group?
Reading Comprehension: Name one other word you see or hear in the story.
Reading Comprehension: Which target word appears near the end of the story?

video.title: Fruits: See It, Say It
video.idea: 30–50 second contextual video set in a market. Show fig, olive, avocado, persimmon, and pomegranate naturally, pause once for the learner to identify a word, then reveal the answer.
video.scriptStarter: Look closely. I can see fig, olive, and avocado. What can you find next?
